root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point()` treats a large non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` as a chaining point and enters the split body, that candidate gap node must have both a left sibling and a right sibling in the concat list.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable guard admits the witness gap from `.{369}? ` even though it is the first concat child and therefore has no left sibling. That missing precondition lets the split body seed the remainder AST with a head pointer to `child`, then free that same node before the second split call reloads it.

nodes.state: After the vulnerable split rewiring on the first-child gap, the newly returned remainder AST keeps `(*remainder_re_ast)->root_node->children_head` pointing at the selected `child` node.
The same `child` node still reachable from the remainder AST head is passed to `yr_re_node_destroy(child)`, ending that node's lifetime.
In the second split call, `child` is reloaded from the remainder AST's `children_head`; the next `child->greedy` test is the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-use-after-free read.

edges.relation: The stale remainder-AST head aliases the exact `child` pointer that `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point()` immediately frees.

The exact node freed by `yr_re_node_destroy(child)` is later reloaded from the remainder AST head in the second `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point()` call, so the sink executes after the free on the same node.
